comment: Matched-pair probes. kind 'true-far' = violates the axiom's principle in code unlike its example (truth: the axiom). kind 'false-near' = echoes the example's surface but violates nothing the axiom asserts (truth: null).

probes.text: When the CSV import hits a duplicate row, the service responds to the API consumer with status 422 and body {} — the consumer gets no indication of which row collided or what uniqueness rule would have been satisfied.
The pagination resolver rejects malformed cursors with { code: 'E_CURSOR' } — an opaque code that tells the API consumer nothing about what a valid cursor looks like or how to obtain one.
The debug log prints 'bad subject' each time newsletter dispatch retries — operator-facing log lines here should include the retry count and backoff delay.
The message 'rating must be a whole number from 1 to 5' differs in tone from the marketing copy on the pricing page — product wants friendlier phrasing across the app.

A caller of archiveParlor cannot discover from its header that a parlor with active subscriptions is refused — that failure surfaces only as a thrown string deep in the body, so callers must read the implementation to handle it.

The header comment says only 'sends the weekly digest' — a caller wiring this into the scheduler has no way to know it can refuse on an empty recipient list or on a rate-limit window without reading the body.
The doc comment enumerating failure modes runs past 15 lines, pushing the function signature below the fold in most editors — consider a tighter layout.
The doc comment lists failure modes as prose sentences while the other services use bulleted 'Fails if:' lists — the formatting is inconsistent across the directory.
Reading describe('loyalty') → it('happy') in the runner output, a reviewer cannot reconstruct which observable outcome distinguishes success from failure.
The assertion group is titled '✓ ok path' — combined with its parent block 'rankParlors', the runner output names no behavior a reader could verify against the spec.
The it block 'returns true for a valid subject' re-seeds the store inline although the surrounding beforeEach already seeds identical parlors — the redundant setup slows the suite.
The it description 'returns the winner list sorted by score' is accurate, but the block asserts on the private comparator helper instead of the returned list itself.
